2026 1.title: The Evening Mallard (Logo)
text: Used a pen tablet (those little slabs of plastic you plug into a computer) and Krita to make this one.
I first photoshopped a picture of a Mallard until it looked kinda like this, then I copied it and then drew a top hat on top.
Used pixlr to photoshop the duck, then to arrange the logo text.

2026 2.title: View from a Park
text: Made with watercolours on regular A4 print paper folded in half.
My first attempt at painting with watercolours. Not too shabby considering.

2026 3.title: Copy of: J.M.W. Turner - Ariccia Sunset
text: On today's episode of butchering artwork!

No, of course I had no expectations going in that I'd be able to match Turner's artwork. This is my first copy of a painting, and it was an interesting experience especially considering I don't really know what I'm doing.
Unlike, say, digital or pencil (where you can undo or erase mistakes), watercolour is much more unforgiving, so any mistake I make is terribly obvious.
Also, yes, I copied an oil painting with watercolours, I'm aware.
I think the sky turned out pretty well though.
This was done using actual watercolour paper: A5, cold-pressed, medium coarse grain specifically.

2026 4.title: Copy of: J.M.W. Turner - Venice by Moonlight, with Boats off a Campanile
text: Yep, Turner again.
This time, I chose to actally copy a watercolour painting and one with a distinctly more 'wet' look.
That big brown splotch to the centre-left is real bad and the sky is a bit too dull, but overall it's OK enough, I think.
However, I didn't really think my choice of canvas through... I used half a page of scrap A5 print paper.

2026 5.title: Copy of: John Constable - View Over a Hilly Country, With a Stormy Sky
text: Constable's watercolour (sketches) were very different to Turner's, so I wanted to give it a go.
Soon, I'm going to actually follow a proper tutorial and stuff, but right now, I'm just seeing what I can pull off.
This was also done on half a page of A5 print paper. I really struggled with getting the dark colours of the original, as you can probably tell.
